newsitem.title: CANADA: Slocan plans lumber production cutback.
newsitem.headline: Slocan plans lumber production cutback.

text.p: Slocan Forest Products Ltd said on Thursday it plans to reduce lumber production through temporary shutdowns at about 10 sawmills in August.
"We are going to be taking all our mills down for at least a week in August," Slocan Chief Financial Officer Ron Price said in a telephone interview.

He said that would involve about 10 mills but was unable to quantify the size of the cutback. But he said market estimates that it would total 30 million to 35 million board feet of lumber were "reasonable."
The exact schedule of the shutdowns had not been worked out but several mills would likely be shut simultaneously, Price said.
Slocan took the decision because of lumber market conditions and export restrictions to the United States under a softwood trade agreement, he said.
After a recent acquisition, Slocan is believed to be Canada's biggest lumber producer with annual capacity of more than 1.6 billion board feet.
Rumors of the cutbacks propelled lumber futures in Chicago sharply higher today.
Lumber analyst Charles Widman said oversupply prompted lumber prices to weaken recently, thus making the shutdowns a logical step.

"It doesn't surprise me with the way lumber prices are dropping. Everybody was overproducing," added another forestry analyst who declined to be identified. "They are trying to match supply and demand."

Finlay Forest Industries Inc, jointly owned by Slocan and Donohue Inc DHC.TO, recently announced it was extending a two-week sawmill shutdown by a week and analysts said International Forest Products Ltd was also taking downtime.
But West Fraser Timber Ltd, which has annual capacity of 1.6 billion board feet and is one of Canada's top producers, did not plan cutbacks, Vice President Gerry Miller said.
